title: C2359 — Instrument panel center speaker connector
introduction:
I use this page to trace the center speaker’s connector labels into the audio circuit table and then into the pigtail records. The useful distinction here is speaker polarity: the plus and minus labels give the connections different roles even though they share a housing. It is a tiny seating plan with an audio assignment for each seat.

Start with the connector identity, locate a cavity in the drawing, and read its complete table row. The final sections provide standard and European service-part references. This page does not teach speaker access, probing or replacement; physical viewing direction, electrical test values, gauge convention and the meaning of the Size code are also outside its identification scope.

edits.why: I use the prominent upper housing feature to keep the drawing’s orientation consistent while matching its side-by-side cavity labels to the table. Left and right here describe the image only. The drawing is not explicitly identified as a terminal-side or wire-side view, so it cannot by itself establish a physical probing orientation.

Match the cavity label first, then read across the circuit identifier, color, gauge, function and terminal fields. The plus and minus function labels distinguish the center speaker’s audio connections. I keep that polarity distinction intact: a speaker-minus label is not an instruction to connect the wire to chassis ground. The assignments alone cannot establish speaker or audio-module condition.

Cross-reference Kit List with Number and Hard Shell with Engineering Shell to connect the connector identity to this pigtail entry. Service Part is the service-item reference; the image filename is a catalog reference. The pigtail and circuit tables have separate gauge entries, which should not be converted into a wire-substitution instruction.

This section provides a European Product Id separately from the preceding service-part record. I retain that distinction when reading the catalog information. The identifier alone does not establish interchangeability or a replacement method.
